proofLimits: Two new public browser journeys use actually earned learner state and actual downloaded calendar bytes. Browser-controlled dates are not natural wall-time delivery.
Twenty-two anonymous source-byte asset observations bind the eleven public paths before/after; deployment metadata alone is not browser proof.
The old sixteen learning paths, nineteen VM identities and three worker journeys remain separate and are not rerun.
Only Playwright1.64.1 is installed in owned runner storage. Chromium Linux system packages belong to the disposable runner.
Exit/close/EOF/groups and same-UID owned browser binary/profile paths plus Linux starttime prove scoped cleanup, not a host-wide inventory.
Calendar-client import/alerts, OS notification delivery, devices and full-product acceptance remain outside this packet.
Full source guards cover the clean pinned CI checkout, not a claim that the separate native checkout's five preserved dirty paths are clean.

cases.title: earned daily progress and due reviews survive the next local day and reload
two actual calendar downloads retain complete recurring local-time event bytes

proofLimits: Two fresh contexts use the canonical public origin; no local server or response fulfillment is used.
C01 uses Playwright 1.64.1 context clock control, not elapsed overnight time, OS clock changes or physical-device/DST acceptance.
Clock installation precedes app navigation. Fixed Date values and runFor execute the existing minute timer; no visibility event or internal app function is invoked.
Only actual UI reviews create progress; only the authored context state key is read. No score, progress or storage state is injected.
C02 reads two complete native browser download files. Calendar import, calendar-client alerts, OS notification delivery and notification enrollment are not exercised.
Default Unicode content and physical UTF-8 line limits are checked; multibyte folding-edge coverage remains separate pure-source evidence.
No closed course, VM, worker-fault, offline, backup, model, account or full mobile-acceptance scope is rerun.
The outer controller owns process attribution, public asset byte checks, source guards and final root removal.
